concerns.text: The plan cites 'MTLD' (https://huggingface.co/datasets/Abeyankar/mtl_ds_full_fin/...) as a 'Reference for lexical diversity validation'. This is a category error: MTLD (Measure of Textual Lexical Diversity) is a calculation algorithm/metric, not a dataset. Citing a dataset named 'mtl_ds' to 'calibrate' the MTLD calculation is inappropriate; the metric is computed from the prompt text itself (IA-Bench/WISE-Verified). If this dataset contains pre-computed MTLD scores for validation, the plan must explicitly state that it is using it for *ground-truth comparison* of the implementation, not 'calibration'. As written, it implies a misunderstanding of the metric's nature.

The plan assumes IA-Bench and WISE-Verified contain 'visual domain' metadata (photorealistic, abstract, illustration) to satisfy FR-010 (Stratified Analysis). The plan states: 'If the datasets lack explicit... metadata... the plan will attempt to infer it from prompt keywords'. This is a high-risk assumption. If the datasets are purely text-prompt pairs without image-domain labels, the 'stratified regression' (FR-010) becomes impossible to execute as a primary analysis, forcing a fallback to keyword heuristics which may not align with the 'visual domain' hypothesis. The plan should verify the schema of IA-Bench/WISE-Verified for explicit domain tags before committing to this analysis path.

The plan resolves the lack of generated images by assuming a 'deterministic mock image generation (e.g., noise pattern or fixed template)'. This fundamentally breaks the 'Context Fidelity' metric (FR-004). CLIP measures semantic similarity between an image and text. A noise pattern or fixed template has no semantic relationship to the prompt text. Therefore, the CLIP score will be near-random or zero for all prompts, making the 'Fidelity Delta' meaningless. The hypothesis (that rule-based expansion preserves fidelity) cannot be tested if the 'generated' images are semantically void. The plan must either: (1) use a real, CPU-tractable image generator (e.g., a small Stable Diffusion model on CPU, even if slow), or (2) use a pre-existing dataset of prompt-image pairs where the 'agent' vs 'rule-based' distinction is simulated via text-only metrics (if applicable), or (3) abandon the CLIP fidelity metric in favor of a text-only coherence metric (BLEU/ROUGE) if image generation is truly out of scope. The current 'mock image' approach invalidates the core measurement.
